summary.headline: Pace Digitek Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 51.3% YoY to Rs.555 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated on Rs.10,803 crore executable order book.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.555 crore (up 51.3% YoY) but down sharply from Rs.1,097 crore in Q4 FY26, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition and a high Q4 base. EBITDA was Rs.86.1 crore (15.5% margin vs 14.9% in Q4) and PAT was Rs.63 crore (11.3% margin vs Rs.55 crore in Q1 FY26). Order inflow in the quarter was about Rs.1,677 crore, with two energy EPC wins (NLC, DVC, ~Rs.1,412 crore) and a BSNL OFC project (~Rs.265 crore). Management said the 5 GWh BESS line is operational, with a further 5 GWh line due to be commissioned by December 2026, and reiterated the FY27 revenue guidance.

segments.name: Energy (BESS, renewable EPC, BOO)
segments.commentary: Contributed 79.5% of Q1 revenue and is the main growth driver; energy executable order book Rs.8,453 crore, split Rs.4,074 crore BOO and Rs.4,367 crore EPC. Management expects energy to be about 65-70% of the order book by year end.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT (BharatNet, Railway Kavach, BSNL OFC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 20.5% of Q1 revenue; executable order book Rs.2,350 crore. Kavach about 30% complete; BSNL OFC (~Rs.265 crore) to execute over about 2.5 years. Management said telecom has better margins but lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore reiterated; management said it sees no concern in achieving it, with most revenue expected from the existing order book.
H1 FY27 targeted at 40-45% of full-year revenue vs 35% in H1 FY26.
Q2 container supply planned at 210 units; management expects about 125+ containers per month in the next calendar year.
FY27 PAT margin guidance of 10.5-11% for BESS, with the lithium-ion cell cost increase said to be factored in.
Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive by March 2027; inventory and receivables expected to stabilise between December and March.
Energy-to-telecom order book mix expected to move to about 65:35 or 70:30 by year end.
capex_capacity: BESS capacity is 5 GWh operational (two 2.5 GWh lines); a third 5 GWh line is due for installation in October 2026, targeting 10 GWh by early December 2026 as India's largest operational BESS facility.
Total capex of about Rs.300 crore for the 5 GWh expansion phase, the container fabrication unit, and related setup, mainly land cost, funded from the earlier private placement.
In-house container manufacturing started with trials this month; batch production from next month. Over 300 containers supplied to date.

BOO projects: 975 MWh commissioned to date (MSEDCL standalone BESS, about Rs.900 crore recognised in P&L); four BOO projects expected to add about Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all are commissioned.
Pune R&D centre inaugurated about three weeks ago; cell manufacturing planning under way. Applying for 4 GWh under the government cell PLI scheme (10 GWh total scheme).
demand_pricing: Bidding for about 27 GWh of tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy and NTPC Green tenders noted, with NTPC Green tenders drawing only 7-8 bidders versus 32-51 in earlier state tenders.
Management said bidding aggression has eased after a 4 GWh Maharashtra project was cancelled and a Punjab tender saw a single bid at higher prices.
Management said cell cost is about 60% of total BESS cost, unchanged; recent tenders include price variation clauses while older tenders do not. Stock was built in March to lower Q1 cell costs.

C&I BESS (below 5 MWh) received product approval from large Indian customers; first trial order of about 25 units, with management referring to potential for thousands per year. Management guided C&I EBITDA margin about 4-5 points above grid-scale product margin of 13-15%.
Container unit value about Rs.4-4.5 crore; about 70 containers per month currently.
Early exports: small container supply to a Saudi company in Q1 and an MoU signed in Saudi Arabia.
MEGMEET tie-up for AI data-centre power solutions in India; demo equipment planned; management said a concrete revenue plan could come in about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Telecom & ICT order inflow break-up and execution timeline for the Rs.2,350 crore telecom book?
qa_highlights.answer: Of Rs.1,677 crore inflow, NLC and DVC EPC wins were about Rs.1,412 crore and BSNL OFC about Rs.265 crore. EPC projects run about one year; OFC about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not higher given the energy order book visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: BOO solar-plus-BESS capex is capitalised as a fixed asset and not recognised as revenue, so physical execution will exceed reported revenue. Revenue recognition comes from EPC and standalone BESS in BOO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow and working-capital profile by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom net working capital is about 5 months (~150 days); energy is expected at 90-100 days. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue path needed from Q2 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the remaining Rs.2,700 crore should come from the existing order book, with Q1 seasonally low due to government funding and approval cycles.

qa_highlights.question: How will rising lithium-ion cell prices affect EPC and BOO margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 10.5-11% margin already includes anticipated cell price increases; price variation clauses in new tenders and stock built in March mitigate impact.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 must deliver roughly Rs.900-1,000 crore to hit H1 at 40-45% of the Rs.3,200-3,400 crore guidance; management has not given a quarterly split beyond H1 share
Commissioning of the third 5 GWh BESS line (October-November 2026) and 10 GWh operational by early December 2026; equipment arrival end-September 2026
Lithium-ion cell cost (about 60% of BESS cost) and exposure in older tenders without price variation clauses; guidance of 10.5-11% PAT margin assumes anticipated cell price increases
Operating cash flow negative; management expects it positive by March 2027, with inventory and receivables stabilising between December and March
Container output ramp from about 70 per month to 210 per quarter in Q2 and 125+ per month next calendar year; in-house container batch production starts next month
Bidding aggression easing after Maharashtra 4 GWh cancellation; watch NTPC Green tender bidder counts and pricing in roughly 27 GWh of bids
BOO expansion depends on securing investors for the portfolio; management said BOO requires significant funding
Pending outcomes: Pune cell PLI application for 4 GWh, AI data-centre tie-up with MEGMEET (concrete revenue plan promised in about one quarter), and Saudi export revenue
key_quotes: I believe that we are absolutely on track and there are no concerns with respect to the business outlook as well as the execution capabilities.
Achieving this year's revenue target of Rs.3,200 -3,400 crore, I do not see any concern at all.
We do not want you to look at mix from the perspective of a fixed percentage.

We will not need any technical partnership for this because we already have our plant running 24 hours, and we have our internal teams, we have selected the right suppliers for these equipments and all.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on order book visibility and FY27 guidance, saying it sees no concern in achieving Rs.3,200-3,400 crore. It was more cautious on Q1 seasonality and cash flow, and it declined to give a fixed energy-telecom mix, saying it does not want investors to view mix as a fixed percentage.

adds.what: Third 5 GWh BESS line (5 GWh expansion to 10 GWh total)
In-house container manufacturing unit (batch production from next month; ~70 containers/month currently, 210 units planned in Q2)
Four BOO projects expected to add ~Rs.750 crore annual revenue once all commissioned

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs.3,200-3,400 crore (midpoint ~21% over FY26 implied by ~Rs.2,700 crore base) reiterated, backed by Rs.10,803 crore executable order book and a third 5 GWh BESS line due ~October-December 2026, though Q1 revenue of Rs.555 crore is well below the run-rate needed and no quarterly capacity utilisation was stated.
